conversation_summary: CIRA completed most intake sections in a calm, orderly manner and appropriately flagged the current passive suicidal thoughts. However, it missed important follow-ups about the overdose/admission and additional repeatable entries, especially the brother’s family history. Several questions were duplicated verbatim, and the current-safety question bundled two concepts.
record_summary: The record is factually strong, clearly organized, and contains accurate PHQ-9 and GAD-7 item scores, totals, difficulty ratings, and safety flag. Its main omissions are the brother’s substance-use disorders and the impulsive overdose as the reason for the admission/suicide attempt. No meaningful fabrication was identified.

issues.evidence: After the patient disclosed, “my sister has panic disorder and depression,” CIRA asked only for additional details about the sister and never asked whether any other family members had psychiatric or substance-use conditions.
issues.explanation: This prevented disclosure of the brother’s alcohol and cocaine use disorder and violated the requirement to ask about additional repeatable entries.

issues.evidence: CIRA asked for admission “year, location, and length of stay” but did not ask the reason for admission; after “one previous suicide attempt,” it also did not ask how the attempt occurred.
issues.explanation: The impulsive overdose was a clinically important supplied fact and should have been elicited as the admission reason or attempt method.

issues.evidence: After recording one diagnosis, one hospital admission, and one job, CIRA moved on without asking whether there were any additional diagnoses, admissions, or jobs.
issues.explanation: These are repeatable fields for which explicit additional-entry checks were required, even though the scenario contained no further entries in those categories.

issues.evidence: “Have you ever been assessed by a mental health professional?” and “Are you currently taking any prescribed medications?” were each repeated twice in the same message; PHQ-9 Question 1 and its instructions were also duplicated.
issues.explanation: These verbatim duplicates violate the one-question/ask-once requirements and add unnecessary friction.

issues.evidence: “Is this something you are experiencing right now, and are you currently able to stay safe?”
issues.explanation: This bundles current ideation and ability to stay safe into one question. The response clarified passive thoughts and no plan but did not directly answer the ability-to-stay-safe component.

issues.evidence: CIRA told the patient, “The patient endorsed PHQ-9 question 9 with a score above 0 and disclosed passive suicidal thoughts.”
issues.explanation: This sounds like internal documentation exposed in the patient-facing dialogue. The safety flag itself was appropriate, but this wording was unnatural.

issues.evidence: The family record contains only “Relationship: Sister” and omits the brother’s alcohol and cocaine use disorder.
issues.explanation: A complete supplied family-history entry is missing because CIRA did not ask about additional family members.

issues.evidence: The record says “Depression after a breakup and a recent hospitalization” and “June 2026, St. Michael's Hospital, 7 days,” without documenting the impulsive overdose as the presenting problem or admission reason.
issues.explanation: The overdose is a relevant supplied fact and an important part of the recent admission and suicide-attempt history.
